summary:
S.U.N.A IV is an interactive planetary platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, uniting real Martian science with gamified exploration.

It delivers a dual-scale digital twin: a global 3D Cesium globe featuring actual rover paths and InSight lander audio, transitioning seamlessly into a 20-meter 2D regional map of Jezero Crater. Integrating NASA MOLA elevation, CTX and HiRISE imagery, and USGS SIM 3464 geological units, the platform lets users inspect slope, roughness, and surface hazards.

At its core, the engine computes optimal, terrain-aware walking traverses between chosen waypoints using A* pathfinding; deriving exact distances, elevation changes, estimated travel times in Martian sols, and MEDA atmospheric assessments. Complementing the GIS tools, an illustrated 2D survival mode lets players navigate Jezero, manage suit vitals, scan ancient lakebeds, and conduct field research.
details:
About the Project

S.U.N.A IV is an interactive planetary exploration platform that combines real Martian scientific data, intelligent route planning, and gamified exploration.

The platform features a global 3D Mars globe and a detailed 2D regional map of Jezero Crater. Users can explore actual rover traverses, visualize geological formations, inspect terrain characteristics, and select starting points and destinations to generate terrain-aware walking routes using the A* pathfinding algorithm.

Behind the scenes, we divide the study area into a grid with a spatial resolution of 20 meters. Each cell contains elevation, slope, roughness, geological classification, movement cost, and navigation validity information. When moving between cells, the routing engine considers distance, terrain difficulty, and elevation changes while excluding areas classified as impassable.

The platform also features an interactive 2D survival game where players explore Martian landscapes, manage spacesuit vitals, scan geological formations, collect samples, and unlock scientific discoveries.

Its mission is to transform raw Martian planetary data into accessible, intuitive, and interactive tools:

  • Scientific Exploration: Enable users to explore Mars from a global orbital perspective down to a detailed 20-meter regional terrain grid.
  • Actionable Path Planning: Generate terrain-aware traverses across Jezero Crater based on elevation, slope, roughness, and surface hazards.
  • Environmental Awareness: Incorporate historical Martian atmospheric observations to provide environmental context for exploration.
  • Gamified Immersion: Translate astronaut field science, sample collection, scanning, and life-support management into an engaging RPG-style experience.

https://github.com/aarogyathapa098/Zero_Requiem

Benefits

  • Demonstrates why the shortest route on Mars is not necessarily the easiest or most suitable.
  • Integrates multiple planetary datasets into a unified exploration platform.
  • Provides estimated travel times, route distances, elevation profiles, and terrain difficulty assessments.
  • Makes complex planetary science and geospatial data accessible through interactive visualizations.
  • Encourages scientific curiosity through exploration, discovery, and resource management.
  • Allows users to compare shortest-distance and lowest-traversal-cost routes.

Impact

  • Helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts understand how real Martian data can inform exploration and mission-planning decisions.
  • Demonstrates how planetary science, geospatial analysis, and computational algorithms can work together to support future human exploration.
  • Bridges the gap between publicly available scientific datasets and interactive educational experiences.
  • Raises awareness of the environmental and logistical challenges associated with exploring Mars.
  • Maintains scientific transparency by distinguishing real observations, derived calculations, simulated conditions, and fictional gameplay.

S.U.N.A IV is an educational and experimental prototype, not an operationally validated astronaut navigation or safety system.

Tools

  • Frontend Core: React 19, TypeScript, Vite.
  • 3D Visualization: CesiumJS with a Mars-specific planetary reference system, Three.js, React Three Fiber.
  • 2D Mapping & Raster Processing: OpenLayers, GeoTIFF.js, HTTP range streaming, and Vite/Node.js middleware.
  • Game Development: HTML5 Canvas, interactive 2D exploration, scanning mechanics, and survival systems.
  • Styling & Design: Custom dark-space visual identity, Barlow Condensed and Manrope typography, sci-fi interface elements, and KaTeX-formatted telemetry.
  • Data Processing: Python-based geospatial processing and raster analysis.
  • Routing: Custom A* pathfinding, eight-directional grid navigation, octile-distance heuristics, and Dijkstra-based algorithm validation.
  • Backend Support: Node.js middleware and optional FastAPI services.
  • Data Sources: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), NASA Mars Trek, MOLA, CTX, HiRISE, MEDA, InSight, and USGS Astrogeology.
  • Team Collaboration: GitHub.

Creativity

  • Combines a global 3D planetary explorer, regional scientific mapping system, and interactive survival game within a unified platform.
  • Integrates real Martian terrain data into a grid-based navigation engine rather than relying on predefined roads or paths.
  • Connects every calculated route to its underlying terrain characteristics, allowing users to understand why alternative routes may be more suitable.
  • Incorporates actual Perseverance and Curiosity rover traverses, interactive rover models, and authentic Martian audio captured by NASA's InSight lander.
  • Creates an immersive orbital-to-surface transition inspired by spacecraft entry, descent, and landing.
  • Transforms real planetary science into interactive gameplay through geological scanning, sample collection, scientific discoveries, survival mechanics, and fictional encounters.
  • Uses gamification to make scientific exploration engaging without misrepresenting fictional elements as actual Martian discoveries.

Factors Considered

  • Elevation: Determines terrain height, elevation changes, and ascent/descent profiles.
  • Slope: Identifies steep terrain and influences movement difficulty.
  • Surface Roughness: Estimates terrain unevenness using neighbouring elevation values.
  • Obstacles: Excludes cells classified as impassable under the navigation model.
  • Geology: Identifies geological formations along exploration routes using USGS SIM 3464.
  • Distance: Accounts for movement between neighbouring grid cells, including diagonal movement.
  • Travel Time: Estimates walking duration using terrain-dependent movement-speed assumptions.
  • Martian Gravity: Considers reduced gravity within the simulated astronaut mobility model.
  • Atmospheric Conditions: Provides environmental context through historical NASA MEDA and InSight observations.
  • Life-Support Requirements: Simulates oxygen, suit power, temperature, and radiation-related vitals within the game.
  • Data Resolution and Uncertainty: Recognizes that orbital imagery and elevation models cannot reliably identify every small rock or surface obstacle.
  • Geospatial Consistency: Aligns regional terrain layers using a common grid and Mars-specific map projection.
  • Scientific Accuracy: Clearly distinguishes NASA and USGS observations from derived terrain properties, simulation assumptions, and fictional gameplay.
